title: Large-area CVD Graphene for Photogating-Based Photodetection
authors: D. A. Matienko, D. P. Borisenko, A. Yu. Kuntsevich
abstract: Our work explores large-area CVD graphene as a scalable platform for photodetectors. We show that substrate-induced photogating in graphene/SiO$_2$/Si structures enables a photoconductivity signal in mono-, bi-, and trilayer CVD graphene. The devices respond to illumination with photon energies above the Si band gap and do not respond to telecom frequency, suggesting the photoconductivity mechanism through the photogating. Large sample area and gate voltage-dependent resistivity measurements allow us to prove the dominant role of the photogating directly, demonstrating similarity of the capacitive recharging current and the photoresponse. The sensitivity is the highest (995 A/W) for the monolayer graphene. Increasing the number of graphene layers reduces the sensitivity due to screening and parallel conduction, but can improve detectivity by lowering the noise level. The sensitivity of CVD graphene device depends on fabrication route of photolitography: device with metal contacts fabricated before graphene transfer show higher photoresponce. Thus, our work demonstrate the potential of industrially relevant CVD graphene for sensitive photogating-based photodetectors.
summary: This paper demonstrates that large-area CVD graphene can function as a sensitive photodetector by utilizing a substrate-induced photogating mechanism. Measurements confirm the signal originates from charge trapping in the underlying silicon oxide/silicon structure, not direct absorption in graphene itself. The results establish high sensitivity for monolayer devices and guide future optimization efforts.
main_problem: To explore large-area CVD graphene as a scalable platform for photodetectors by characterizing the underlying photoconductivity mechanism.
main_result: The photoresponse is dominated by substrate-induced photogating in the $	ext{Si}/	ext{SiO}_2/	ext{Si}$ structure, achieving a peak sensitivity of $995 	ext{ A/W}$ for monolayer graphene.
method: Electrical and optical characterization using dual-frequency modulation schemes across various wavelengths to measure photoconductivity and photoresponse dependence on power density.
model_or_system: The physical system is large-area CVD graphene grown on $	ext{Si}/	ext{SiO}_2/	ext{Si}$ substrates. The mechanism relies on photogating, where light absorption in the substrate generates trapped charges that modulate the gate voltage experienced by the graphene channel.
key_observables: Photoconductivity signal; photoresponse ($I_{ph}$) vs. optical power density ($P$); sensitivity ($S$) and detectivity ($D^*$); dependence on graphene layer number (mono-, bi-, tri-layer).
important_parameters: Photon energy relative to the Si band gap; fabrication route (metal contacts before or after transfer); carrier screening effects related to layer count.
main_assumptions: The photogating effect is confirmed as dominant over direct light absorption in graphene, and that device performance depends critically on the fabrication sequence of metal contacts.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate device structure, Raman characterization confirming layer number, and plots comparing photoresponse vs. optical power density for different layer counts and fabrication routes.
paper_structure: The work systematically characterizes the photodetector response by first establishing the mechanism (photogating) using spectral analysis and power dependence, then quantifying performance metrics like sensitivity across varying graphene thicknesses, and finally discussing optimization strategies.
why_interesting: While focused on solid-state photonics, the study involves charge trapping dynamics at interfaces ($	ext{graphene}/	ext{SiO}_2/	ext{Si}$) under illumination, which touches upon open quantum systems concepts related to environmental coupling and decoherence in nanoscale devices.
